subject: Change variable names and sequential outcomes within a loop

messages.author: e16affb65d44d10f
messages.subject: Change variable names and sequential outcomes within a loop
parts:
Hello all,
I am trying to run the same few commands for several objects called PI1, PI2, ... , PI100 (coming from different networks called nw1, ..., nw100).
I dont want to type the same thing 100 times, so I was thinking on doing a loop that covers those 100 objects and their respective outcomes.

As an example, here I have the code used for PI1 and PI2:

sim = 1:100

PI1<-get.vertex.pid(nw1) # Extract the random names of each nodes (1221) in my network 1.
inf<- matrix(0, length(sim), 1221)
for (j in 1:length(sim)){
  for (i in 1:nrow(sim1.SIR$stats$transmat[[j]])){ # number of rows in the transmission matrix, in each j simulation
    inf[j, which(PI1 == sim1.SIR$stats$transmat[[j]]$inf[i])]<- 1 # for simulation j, give a one on the column-location where the specific node is infected
  }
}
sum(inf[1:100,])
R1<-colSums(inf)



PI2<-get.vertex.pid(nw2) # Extract the random names of each nodes (1221) in my network.
inf<- matrix(0, length(sim), 1221)
for (j in 1:length(sim)){
  for (i in 1:nrow(sim1.SIR$stats$transmat[[j]])){ # number of rows in the transmission matrix, in each j simulation
    inf[j, which(PI2 == sim1.SIR$stats$transmat[[j]]$inf[i])]<- 1 # for simulation j, give a one on the column-location where the specific node is infected
  }
}
sum(inf[1:10,])
R2<-colSums(inf)




Now, what I am trying is something like this:

for (k in 1:length(sim)){
  nws<- get_network(sim1.SIR, sim = k)
  assign(paste("nws", k, sep=""),nws)

  PI<-get.vertex.pid(paste("nws", k, sep=""))
  inf<- matrix(0, length(sim), 1221)
  for (j in 1:length(sim)){
   
    for (i in 1:nrow(sim1.SIR$stats$transmat[[j]])){
      inf[j, which(PI1 == sim1.SIR$stats$transmat[[j]]$inf[i])]<-1#Location of the
      }
    R<-colSums(inf)
    assign(paste("R", j, sep=""),R)
  }
}


My expected output would be R1, R2, ..., R100. I do get those names, but all of them have the same value (that of R1).
My nw1 and nws are class "networkDynamic", so I do not know how to get a reproducible example of that. But if you are willing to give it a go, I could share my networks with you.

Thanks!

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Change variable names and sequential outcomes within a loop
parts:
Hi, Esther. I can't claim to have sorted through your impressive
strings of dollar signs and brackets, so I may be missing the point
entirely, but I don't see where you get `PI1` in the `which`
statement, and I don't see how it ever changes.

Also, I wonder if you really need to keep manufacturing variable
names. Why not just have `R` be a vector of length 100 and fill in
R[j] as you go along, for instance?

-- Mike
